Clustering was tried first and rejected on evidence: at one locus the UPGMA 2-cut is unstable (8/16 to 20/24 wolf purity depending on window), because wolf and dog share most variation. What works is the standard ancestry-informative-marker view. The build script now writes AF_wolf/AF_dog per site with `bcftools +fill-tags -S` over the full FLARE panels (36 European wolves, 318 one-per-breed dogs) before the sample subset, and the display filters `AF_wolf>=0.8 && AF_dog<=0.15` -> 21 markers in one 11 kb LD block. Rows: all 12 Greek gray wolves, all 11 painted animals, all 7 German Shepherd-lineage dogs (the breed both wolfdogs were crossed back to; 0-2 of 21 across its 14 haplotypes, so the negative control is clean). Every painted row carries FLARE's own per-haplotype call in its label AND its swatch AND its gutter tint, so a reader checks rows without a callout. featureColor paints alt cells the painting's wolf orange (the default blue collided with the Dog swatch). Result: 34 of 36 non-reference rows follow their call; the two that do not (Saarloos 2 hap2, Saarloos 4 hap2, both called Dog, both filled) are the figure's point -- these markers average AF 0.86 in wolves and 0.098 in dogs, 11.4% of the collection's 3,138 breed-dog haplotypes carry them, so ~1.9 carriers among 17 dog-called haplotypes is the prediction and there are 2. Also fixed a plugin gap this exposed: getVariantLegendSections dropped the cell legend for ANY custom featureColor, but a plain CSS color is exactly the case a key can be built for, so the figure had no key at all. Plain colors now keep the genotype legend with the alt swatch recolored (test added); popgen/in2lt_per_sample gains a Genotypes key it never had and was regenerated.
